sections.section: 1. Definition & Background – Definition (“the systematic discipline concerned with studying, compiling, and managing specialized terms by analyzing concepts to yield clear names”)

A second sense was added: “also the set of terms used in one field”, and the second Arabic name المصطلحية was added to علم المصطلح (first expert review, r4.json item 0). A separate key term ‘Term’ (“a word or expression that names a concept in a special field”) keeps the document’s link between terms and concepts.
sections.reason: Simplified for beginners; the extra sense and Arabic name were added because the handbook uses ‘terminology’ for the set of terms of a field and المصطلحية is the other standard Arabic name (r4.json 0). The definition is now credited to Cabré (1999), a published source, instead of to the team document.

sections.section: 1. Definition & Background – Historical Background: modern field in the 1930s through Eugen Wüster (Vienna School), ‘the founder of modern terminology’

sections.reason: Partly inaccurate as written (report_content.js Section 7.2: ‘Historical claims about the founding of terminology … Checked and corrected, then removed in the beginner revision’); removed as history (Section 8.2).

sections.section: 5. How Terminologists Work – Core role: terminologists work within a single language to coin new terms and establish standardised terminology
sections.where: Chapter 21, Words to remember (‘Terminologist’), Step 2 (second bullet), Try it question 1 and answer
sections.details: Now: “A terminologist studies the terms of a field rather than whole texts: they collect, record and sometimes standardise them, in one or more languages.” The key term reads “A specialist who collects, describes and records the terms of a field, and sometimes standardises them, in one or more languages.” The contrast with translators is kept but changed from ‘two languages vs one language’ to ‘whole texts vs the terms of a field’.
sections.reason: Corrected as a high-severity error in the first expert review: terminologists mainly collect, describe and record terms, and translation-oriented terminology work (UNTERM, IATE, Arabterm) is bilingual or multilingual, so ‘creates … usually in one language’ misdescribes the job (r4.json items 1, 2 and 9). The final report lists ‘the definition of a terminologist’ among the important corrections. Earlier versions (c2b_v3.js) had followed the document.
